Setup and Credentials

Source: vignettes/setup.Rmd
setup.Rmd

Use this page once before the homepage quick example or the 5-Minute Quickstart.

It covers three things:

  1. GitHub credentials so remotes::install_github() works reliably.
  2. Optional setup for having a model review the semantic shortlists in your own harness.
  3. Short-lived DataONE credentials for an explicit live KNB deposit.

1) GitHub setup for installs and updates

metasalmon is installed from GitHub. Public installs often work without a token, but setting up a GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT) up front avoids rate limits and awkward auth failures.

Create a GitHub token

Create a PAT in GitHub:

  • https://github.com/settings/tokens

For public package install/update, a read-only token is enough. If you also plan to read private GitHub repositories later, make sure the token can access those repositories too.

Store it in ~/.Renviron 

file.edit("~/.Renviron")

Add:

GITHUB_PAT="paste token here"

Restart R after saving.

Install metasalmon 

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("salmon-data-mobilization/metasalmon")

If you also need private GitHub CSV access later

The install token and the package’s private-repo CSV helpers are related but not identical workflows.

When you later want to use read_github_csv() against a private repository, run:

ms_setup_github(repo = "your-org/your-private-repo")

That verifies private GitHub access for the repository you actually intend to read.

2) Optional: model review in your own harness

The base quick example and quickstart need no API key, and neither does the package at any point: metasalmon makes no model call. When you want a model to judge the ontology candidates the package found, the judgement runs in your own harness (for example Claude Code or Codex), against a review packet the package writes and reads back. That needs:

  • the sdp-semantic-review skill from the public smn-sci-plgn plugin (release v0.2.0 or later), installed in your harness as the plugin’s README describes, or a harness of your own that follows the packet’s instructions;
  • nothing in R beyond metasalmon itself. HTML, DOCX, .R, .Rmd and .qmd context files need no extra package; for the packet to quote your PDF or Excel files, install the optional readers once:
install.packages(c("pdftools", "readxl"))

Any credential your harness uses for its model is the harness’s own configuration, not something metasalmon reads. Semantic Review in Your Harness walks through the whole route.

3) Optional DataONE/KNB live-deposit credential

You do not need a DataONE credential to build EML or create a KNB dry-run manifest. For a live deposit, sign in to DataONE with the same ORCID recorded as the single EML metadata provider and obtain a short-lived DataONE JWT.

Treat this token differently from an install PAT. Do not put it in .Renviron, a script, a command argument, an EML sidecar, a publication manifest, or a transformation record. Enter it only into the current R process and clear it immediately afterward:

options(dataone_token = rstudioapi::askForPassword("Short-lived DataONE JWT"))
on.exit(options(dataone_token = NULL), add = TRUE)

The live KNB preflight verifies that DataONE reports the authenticated subject as the metadata-provider ORCID. A matching string supplied locally is not enough.
